comment: The household exercise plan for wger, read by gen_wger.py (runbook docs/runbooks/workout-tracking-update.md). Built-in wger exercises only, keyed by uuid; name = the English name wger must report for that uuid. how/safety/video become the exercise's description. Doses, rest and start weights (lb) live in the routines. No pain notes or medical history here: the vault holds those.

treadmill-walk.name: Treadmill Cardio
how: Start with 3-5 minutes at an easy pace.
Walk tall with a relaxed arm swing; touch the rails only for balance.
Hold a pace where you can still talk in full sentences.
Progress one thing at a time: a little more incline or pace from week to week.
Finish with 2-3 easy minutes.
treadmill-walk.safety: Clip on the safety key; stand on the side rails while the belt starts or stops. Walking only: no running, no intervals.

goblet-squat.name: Dumbbell Goblet Squat
how: Hold one dumbbell vertically at your chest, elbows tucked; stand in front of the bench, feet shoulder-width.
Sit the hips back and down until you lightly touch the bench.
Keep the chest up and the knees tracking over the toes.
Stand up by pushing the floor away through the whole foot.
goblet-squat.safety: Squat to the bench, not below it; no bouncing. Stop the set if a knee hurts.

db-rdl.name: Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift
how: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand in front of the thighs, knees soft (never locked).
Push the hips back and slide the weights down the front of the legs.
Keep the back flat and the weights close; stop when the hamstrings are tight.
Squeeze the glutes and drive the hips forward to stand.
db-rdl.safety: Stop the descent before the lower back rounds; start light.

step-up.name: Step-ups
how: Place one whole foot on a sturdy, low bench or step.
Lean slightly forward and press through that heel to stand up on it.
Bring the other foot up, then step down slowly with the same order reversed.
Finish all reps on one leg, then switch.
step-up.safety: Start with a low step and bodyweight; step, never jump. Stop if the knee hurts.

db-hip-thrust.name: Dumbbell Hip Thrust
how: Sit on the floor with the upper back against the side of the bench, one dumbbell across the hips.
Feet flat, about hip-width, close enough that the shins are vertical at the top.
Tuck the chin and drive the hips up until the body is flat from shoulders to knees.
Squeeze the glutes for a second, then lower under control.
db-hip-thrust.safety: Do not arch the lower back at the top; hold the dumbbell steady with both hands.

calf-raise.name: Standing Calf Raises
how: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand, feet hip-width.
Rise onto the balls of the feet as high as you can.
Pause one second at the top.
Lower slowly until the heels touch down.
calf-raise.safety: Use a wall or door frame for balance if needed; move slowly, no bouncing.

tib-raise.name: Tibialis raises
how: Lean your back against a wall with the heels about a foot in front of it.
Keep the legs straight and lift the toes as high as you can.
Pause at the top, then lower slowly without slapping the feet down.
Step the feet further out to make it harder.
tib-raise.safety: A burn in the shins is normal; stop if it turns into sharp pain.

plank.name: Plank
how: Forearms on the mat, elbows under the shoulders.
Step the feet back so the body is one straight line from head to heels.
Brace the stomach and squeeze the glutes.
Breathe steadily for the whole hold.
plank.safety: End the hold when the hips sag or the lower back aches.

dead-bug.name: Deadbug
how: Lie on your back, arms straight up, hips and knees bent to 90 degrees.
Press the lower back gently into the mat.
Slowly reach one arm overhead and the opposite leg out long.
Return and repeat on the other side.
dead-bug.safety: Only go as far as you can keep the lower back down; move slowly.

bird-dog.name: Bird Dog
how: Start on hands and knees, hands under the shoulders, knees under the hips.
Brace the stomach and keep the back flat.
Reach one arm forward and the opposite leg back until both are level with the body.
Pause, return slowly and switch sides.
bird-dog.safety: Keep the hips level and do not arch the back; use a mat under the knees.

incline-db-press.name: Incline Bench Press - Dumbbell
how: Set the bench to a low incline (about 30 degrees).
Sit back with a dumbbell in each hand at the chest, shoulder blades pulled back.
Press the weights up and slightly in until the arms are straight.
Lower under control to the sides of the chest.
incline-db-press.safety: Keep the feet planted and the elbows about 45 degrees from the body; lower the weights to the thighs to finish.

chest-supported-row.name: Incline Chest-Supported Dumbbell Row
how: Set the bench to an incline and lie chest-down on it, a dumbbell in each hand.
Let the arms hang straight down.
Pull the elbows back toward the hips, squeezing the shoulder blades together.
Lower slowly to a full stretch.
chest-supported-row.safety: Keep the chest on the pad and the neck relaxed; do not shrug.

db-shoulder-press.name: Shoulder Press, Dumbbells
how: Sit on the bench set upright, a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height.
Brace the stomach and keep the back against the pad.
Press the weights overhead until the arms are straight.
Lower under control back to the shoulders.
db-shoulder-press.safety: Do not lean back or arch to finish a rep; stop on shoulder pain.

lateral-raise.name: Lateral Raises
how: Stand with a light dumbbell in each hand at your sides, elbows slightly bent.
Raise the arms out to the sides up to shoulder height.
Lead with the elbows and keep the shoulders down.
Lower slowly.
lateral-raise.safety: Use light weights and no swinging; stop at shoulder height.

hammer-curl.name: Hammer Curls
how: Stand with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing each other.
Keep the elbows pinned at your sides.
Curl the weights up toward the shoulders without turning the wrists.
Lower slowly to straight arms.
hammer-curl.safety: No swinging or leaning back; lighten the weight if you have to.

overhead-triceps.name: Triceps Overhead (Dumbbell)
how: Sit tall and hold one dumbbell overhead with both hands under the top plate.
Keep the upper arms close to the head.
Lower the weight behind the head by bending the elbows.
Straighten the arms to lift it back up.
overhead-triceps.safety: Brace the stomach so the back does not arch; control the weight behind the head.

side-plank.name: Side Plank
how: Lie on your side with the elbow under the shoulder, legs stacked.
Lift the hips so the body is a straight line from head to feet.
Hold, breathing steadily, then switch sides.
Easier: bend the knees and keep them on the mat.
side-plank.safety: End the hold when the hips drop; keep the neck in line with the spine.

suitcase-carry.name: Suitcase Carry
how: Pick up one dumbbell at your side, like a suitcase.
Stand tall: do not lean toward or away from the weight.
Walk slowly with short, even steps for the set length.
Put it down with a squat, then carry it on the other side.
suitcase-carry.safety: Clear the walking path first; lift and set the weight down with a flat back.

reverse-crunch.name: Reverse crunch
how: Lie on your back, knees bent, hands flat by your sides.
Use the stomach to curl the hips off the mat, knees toward the chest.
Lower the hips slowly until the feet almost touch down.
Keep the movement small and controlled.
reverse-crunch.safety: No swinging the legs for momentum; keep the neck relaxed on the mat.

split-squat.name: Dumbbell Split Squat
how: Stand in a long stride, back heel up; hold the dumbbells at your sides once bodyweight is easy.
Keep both feet where they are for the whole set: this is stationary, not a walking lunge.
Lower straight down to a comfortable depth, front knee over the middle of the foot.
Push through the front foot to rise; finish the reps, then switch legs.
split-squat.safety: Stationary only, no jumping or pivoting; go only as deep as feels comfortable and stop on knee pain.

sl-rdl.name: Single-Leg Deadlift with Dumbbell
how: Stand on one leg, knee soft, a dumbbell in the opposite hand.
Hinge at the hip and let the free leg rise behind you as the weight lowers.
Keep the hips square to the floor and the back flat.
Stand back up by squeezing the glute of the standing leg.
sl-rdl.safety: Touch a wall or the bench for balance if needed; stop before the back rounds.

wall-sit.name: Wall-sit
how: Lean your back flat against a wall, feet about two feet out.
Slide down to a comfortable depth, knees over the ankles.
Hold, breathing steadily.
Slide back up to finish.
wall-sit.safety: Thighs no lower than parallel; stay higher if a knee complains, and stop on knee pain.

sl-glute-bridge.name: Single Leg Glute Bridge
how: Lie on your back, one knee bent with the foot flat, the other leg straight.
Push through the heel on the floor to lift the hips.
Keep the hips level at the top and squeeze the glute.
Lower slowly; finish the reps, then switch.
sl-glute-bridge.safety: Do not arch the lower back to get higher; if the hamstring cramps, bring the foot closer.

side-lying-abduction.name: Side Lying Hip Abduction
how: Lie on your side, head on your arm, bottom knee bent for balance.
Keep the top leg straight with the toes pointing forward.
Lift the top leg slightly behind the body to about 45 degrees.
Lower slowly.
side-lying-abduction.safety: Do not roll the hips backward; a smaller range done right beats a high kick.

sl-calf-raise.name: Calf raises, one legged
how: Stand on one foot, lightly holding a wall for balance.
Rise onto the ball of the foot as high as you can.
Pause one second, then lower slowly.
Finish the reps, then switch.
sl-calf-raise.safety: Use the wall for balance only, not to lift yourself; no bouncing.

lying-leg-raise.name: Leg Raises, Lying
how: Lie on your back, hands under the hips or flat by your sides.
Press the lower back into the mat.
Raise the legs together, knees soft, until they point at the ceiling.
Lower slowly, stopping before the back lifts.
lying-leg-raise.safety: Bend the knees more if the lower back arches; no swinging.

plank-shoulder-tap.name: Plank Shoulder Taps
how: Start in a high plank, hands under the shoulders, feet wider than the hips.
Brace the stomach and squeeze the glutes.
Lift one hand to tap the opposite shoulder, then put it back down.
Alternate sides, keeping the hips still.
plank-shoulder-tap.safety: Widen the feet or drop to the knees if the hips rock.

hollow-hold.name: Hollow Hold
how: Lie on your back and press the lower back into the mat.
Lift the shoulders and the legs a little off the mat, arms reaching forward or overhead.
Hold the shape, breathing steadily.
Easier: bend the knees or keep the arms by your sides.
hollow-hold.safety: End the hold when the lower back lifts off the mat.

db-bench-press.name: Benchpress Dumbbells
how: Lie on the flat bench, feet planted, a dumbbell in each hand at the chest.
Pull the shoulder blades back and down.
Press the weights up until the arms are straight.
Lower under control to the sides of the chest.
db-bench-press.safety: Keep the elbows about 45 degrees from the body; lower the weights to the thighs to finish.

one-arm-row.name: Bent Over Dumbbell Rows
how: Put one hand and the same-side knee on the bench, back flat.
Hold a dumbbell in the other hand, arm hanging straight down.
Pull the elbow up toward the hip.
Lower slowly; finish the reps, then switch arms.
one-arm-row.safety: Keep the back flat and do not twist the torso to lift the weight.

push-up.name: Push-Up
how: Hands slightly wider than the shoulders, body straight from head to heels.
Lower the chest toward the floor, elbows about 45 degrees from the body.
Push back up to straight arms.
Easier: hands on the bench, or knees down.
push-up.safety: Keep the hips from sagging; stop the set when form breaks.

db-pullover.name: Dumbbell Pullover
how: Lie on the flat bench and hold one dumbbell over the chest with both hands.
Keep a slight bend in the elbows.
Lower the weight back over the head in an arc until you feel a stretch.
Pull it back over the chest.
db-pullover.safety: Go only as far back as the shoulders allow without pain; keep the ribs down.

rear-delt-raise.name: Chest-Supported Rear Delt Raise
how: Lie chest-down on the bench set to an incline, a light dumbbell in each hand.
Let the arms hang, elbows slightly bent.
Raise the arms out to the sides until level with the body.
Lower slowly.
rear-delt-raise.safety: Use light weights; do not shrug or swing.

biceps-curl.name: Biceps Curls With Dumbbell
how: Stand with a dumbbell in each hand, palms forward.
Keep the elbows at your sides.
Curl the weights up toward the shoulders.
Lower slowly to straight arms.
biceps-curl.safety: No swinging or leaning back; lighten the weight if you have to.

triceps-kickback.name: Tricep Dumbbell Kickback
how: Hinge forward with a flat back, one hand on the bench if you like.
Hold the upper arm still along your side, elbow bent to 90 degrees.
Straighten the arm back until it is in line with the body.
Return slowly.
triceps-kickback.safety: Keep the upper arm still and the back flat; use a light weight.

farmer-carry.name: Dumbbell farmer's carry
how: Pick up a dumbbell in each hand with a squat, not a bent back.
Stand tall, shoulders down and back.
Walk slowly with short, even steps for the set time.
Set the weights down with a squat.
farmer-carry.safety: Clear the walking path first; put the weights down before your grip fails.

russian-twist.name: Russian Twist
how: Sit on the mat with knees bent and heels on the floor; lean back slightly with a straight back.
Hold the hands (or a light dumbbell) at the chest.
Turn the chest to one side, then the other, moving from the ribs.
Keep the movement slow.
russian-twist.safety: Keep the feet down and the back straight; stop if the lower back complains.

box-squat.name: Box squat
how: Use a box, bench or chair high enough that your hips sit slightly above your knees.
Stand in front of it, feet shoulder-width.
Sit down fully with control.
Drive through the heels to stand back up.
box-squat.safety: Sit, do not drop; raise the seat if the bottom feels strained.

pallof-press.name: PALLOF PRESS
how: Anchor a band at chest height and stand side-on to it, handle at the chest.
Step away until the band pulls; feet hip-width, knees soft.
Press the handle straight out, hold 2 seconds, bring it back.
Finish the reps, then face the other way.
pallof-press.safety: Do not let the torso twist toward the anchor; check the anchor holds before each set.

incline-push-up.name: Push-Ups | Incline
how: Hands on a wall, a high counter or the bench, slightly wider than the shoulders.
Step back so the body is one straight line.
Lower the chest toward the surface.
Push back up to straight arms.
incline-push-up.safety: No sagging hips or arched back; a higher surface makes it easier.

seated-band-row.name: Rowing seated, narrow grip
how: Sit tall on the floor, legs out, a resistance band looped around the feet.
Hold one end in each hand, arms straight.
Pull the elbows back, squeezing the shoulder blades together.
Return slowly.
seated-band-row.safety: Do not lean back or let the lower back arch; check the band for nicks first.

glute-bridge.name: Glute Bridge
how: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat and hip-width.
Squeeze the glutes to lift the hips into a line from shoulders to knees.
Hold at the top, then lower slowly.
glute-bridge.safety: Do not over-arch the lower back at the top.

walking.name: Walking
how: Walk tall with long, deliberate strides and a relaxed arm swing.
In the pool: chest-deep water, walking forward, backward and sideways.
Keep a moderate pace: you can still hold a conversation.
walking.safety: Pool: enter by the steps and walk where you can stand comfortably.

double-calf-raise.name: Double Leg Calf Raise
how: Stand tall, feet hip-width, a hand on a wall or chair for balance.
Squeeze the glutes for 3 seconds.
Rise slowly onto the balls of both feet and pause 1 second at the top.
Lower slowly.

hip-flexor-stretch.name: Hip Flexor Stretch
how: Kneel tall on a cushion.
Tuck the pelvis under and squeeze the glute on the side you stretch.
Feel the stretch at the front of that hip; hold and breathe.
Do not lunge forward: the stretch comes from the tuck alone.
hip-flexor-stretch.safety: Ease into a mild stretch; never bounce.

wall-squat.name: Wall Squat
how: Stand with your back against a smooth wall, feet a little in front of you.
Slide down into a partial squat, no lower than 90 degrees.
Hold, breathing steadily, then slide back up.
wall-squat.safety: Stay higher if the knees complain; keep the back on the wall.

cow-cat.name: Yoga exercise: Cow-cat
how: Start on hands and knees, hands under the shoulders, knees under the hips.
Breathe out and gently round the back, tucking the tailbone under with the lower stomach.
Breathe in and return to a flat back (or a gentle arch).
Move slowly with the breath.
cow-cat.safety: Stay in a comfortable range; do not let the lower back sag.

jmack.name: Jacob
jmack.about: 30-min treadmill walk, then about 60 min of training; core last. Weights in lb per dumbbell unless the slot says one dumbbell. Progression: when every set reaches the top of the rep range, go up one dumbbell step and start again at the bottom of the range.

rach.name: Rachel
rach.about: Desk breaks and evening mobility every day; Strength A Monday, Strength B Thursday, water walking Tuesday and Friday.

desk.comment: Desk break, 2-3x a day: glute squeeze 3 s, then 15 slow calf raises
Desk break, 2-3x a day: tall-kneeling, pelvis tucked

evening.comment: Supported wall slide: no lower than 90 degrees, hold 5 s each rep
Hands-and-knees pelvic tilt: tuck the tailbone, back to flat
